about: Companion to the files in ./locales. Nothing imports this at runtime — it exists so that whoever writes the next language (person or model) knows where a string appears, what it is allowed to say, and how it is meant to sound.

scripts/checkI18n.ts enforces that it stays honest: every namespace in en.json needs an entry with a non-empty "where", and every shipped locale needs an entry in languageNotes. Adding a namespace without documenting it fails the build.
howToAddALanguage: 1. Copy locales/en.json to locales/<code>.json and translate it. English is the reference: it's where the source strings are authored, and what checkI18n compares against.

2. Add one line to LANGUAGES in i18n/index.ts, labelled with the language's own endonym (Italiano, 日本語 — not "Italian", "Japanese"). resources, supportedLngs and the Settings picker are all derived from that array.
3. Add a languageNotes entry below, covering at least the plural shape and the register you chose.
4. Drop the circular flag for it into i18n/flags/<code>.svg — see the README there for where they come from. It is picked up by filename; a language with no file just shows without one.
5. Run `npm run check:i18n -w web`. It verifies key parity, interpolation parity per plural variant, and this file's coverage.

Plural shape is the one thing that bites. i18next looks up `key_<category>` for the target language and falls back to the bare `key` when that's absent. So: a language with only `other` (Japanese, Chinese) can use bare keys alone; a language with one/other (English, Italian) needs bare + `_other`, because a `_other`-only key resolves to the raw key name at count 1; and `_many` (Spanish, Italian, ≥1,000,000) falls back to the bare *singular* if omitted, which is why sync.offlinePending spells it out.

conventions.interpolation: {{name}}, {{count}}, {{days}}, {{age}}, {{months}}, {{version}} etc. are substituted verbatim. Keep every one the reference uses; word order may move freely around them. checkI18n compares the set per key, treating variables English omits from one plural variant as optional.
conventions.brandNames: Google, Instagram, Xiaohongshu (小红书 — use the Chinese name in zh and ja, the romanised one elsewhere), Groq, OpenRouter, OpenAI, Android, Wi-Fi and API-key placeholders stay as they are.
conventions.examplePlaceholders: Placeholders such as http://spark.local:8000/v1 and qwen3-32b are examples of what to type, not strings to translate.
conventions.ellipsis: Placeholders and in-progress labels use the single character … , not three dots.
conventions.length: These strings sit in chips, buttons and table cells. Aim at or below the English length; a chip truncates with an ellipsis rather than wrapping.
conventions.scripts: Place names and captions are whatever the source wrote — Chinese, English, mixed. Nothing in the UI may assume Latin script, and nothing here should imply the content is in the UI language.

tone.default: Plain, warm, second person, no exclamation marks. This is a private map of places worth your time, not a productivity tool — it should never sound like it is grading the user. Prefer the everyday word over the technical one, except in Settings where precision matters more.
tone.genderNeutrality: {{name}} is any person of unknown gender, and the reader's gender is unknown too. In gendered languages, avoid constructions that force agreement on either: prefer verbs and nouns that don't inflect, restructure rather than pick a default, and never ship a slash form (amico/a).

app.where: The name and one-line strapline, on the sign-in screen and in the browser/app title.

keys.name: The product name. Kept as "Rove" in every language — it is a name, not a word.
keys.tagline: One line under the name. Places first, events second, and the map is the point.

nav.where: Sidebar on desktop, bottom tab bar on phones. Four slots, the tightest space in the app — one word each, no verbs except Add.

keys.add: The intake screen: share a post here or paste a link. A verb is fine — it is the one tab that does something.

auth.where: Sign-in screen, and the sign-out button at the bottom of Settings.

keys.continueWithoutAccount: Starts a local-only copy with no server account. Should sound like a real choice, not a downgrade.

sync.where: A status pill in the header, and toasts when the connection or session state changes.

keys.offlinePending: Counted. Very tight — it sits in a pill beside the header. "Offline" plus a count of queued changes.

update.where: A banner when a new app version is available.

keys.needsInstall: {{version}} is a semver string; keep the literal "v" prefix next to it.

common.where: Shared button and control labels across every dialog, form and toast.

keys.cancel: Dismisses a dialog. In several languages this is the same word as `undo`; that's fine, they never appear together (cancel is in dialogs, undo is in toasts).
keys.undo: The action button on a toast, reversing what just happened.
keys.less: Collapses an expanded list. Pairs with `more`; both must fit a small ghost button.
keys.optional: Lowercase on purpose — it renders inline beside a field label.
keys.skipToContent: The first link on the page, visible only while focused: it jumps a keyboard user past the sidebar. Never seen by most people, but read aloud by screen readers, so it must be a plain instruction rather than a clever one.

map.where: The map screen, which is the home screen. Until the renderer lands it shows an empty state with a count.

keys.emptyDescription: Counted. {{count}} is how many saved places exist and will be drawn.
keys.markerCount: A small counted pill in the map's corner.

list.where: The list screen: every saved item, newest first, and its empty state.

keys.weekend: A toggle beside the filter tabs: only events in the coming Friday-evening-to-Sunday window. Short — it sits on a phone row.
keys.sourcesDown: A warning banner; {{sources}} is a comma-separated list of source names in their own script (豆瓣同城, 秀动).
keys.candidateCount: Screen-reader text for the badge on the List tab, counted.

add.where: The intake screen. Reached from the tab and from the Android share sheet, which arrives with a link already filled.

keys.receivedTitle: Shown above the shared link the moment the share sheet lands, before anything has been fetched.
keys.captionFrom: {{source}} is a source id such as "xiaohongshu-share" or "instagram-oembed", shown as-is.
keys.merged: Shown when a saved link resolves to a place already in the list; {{title}} is that place's name.

items.where: Labels for what an item is (kind) and where it stands (status), shown as small captions on list rows and in filters.

keys.kind.film: A film currently in cinemas. "Film" rather than "movie" in English; the everyday word elsewhere.
keys.status.candidate: Something an automated source found that the user has not yet kept or dismissed. "Suggested" in English, never "pending".
keys.status.dismissed: The user saw it and said no. Neutral — not "rejected".
keys.stars: Screen-reader name of each star in the rating control, counted.
keys.navigate: The button that opens the maps app at the place. One word; "Navigate", "Go", 导航.
keys.keep: Accept a suggestion into the saved list. Pairs with dismiss; both are short buttons.
keys.unkeep: Undo a keep: the saved item goes back to being a suggestion. The opposite of keep, not delete; short button.
keys.openDetails: First entry of an item's right-click menu: opens the full item sheet.
keys.copyName: Right-click menu entry: copies the item's name, as written, to the clipboard.
keys.fromPost: Heading of the item sheet's block quoting the post (an Instagram or 小红书 post, a feed listing) the item was found in.
keys.openPost: Link under that quote: opens the original post in a new tab.
keys.unkeepTitle: Confirm dialog before unkeeping an item you rated, wrote notes on or visited.
keys.unkeepDescription: Why it asks: the item becomes a suggestion again, and suggestions are deleted when they expire, taking the rating, notes and visits with them.
keys.unkept: Toast after unkeep: the item is back among the suggestions.
keys.dismiss: Decline a suggestion. Neutral and personal ("not for me"), never "reject".
keys.findOnMap: Geocode a suggested event's venue text on request; spends one search.

calendar.where: The shared date picker that replaced every native date input: month arrows and the selected-day label.

keys.previous: Screen-reader label on the month arrows, shared by the Calendar page and the date picker. "Month", not "page".

settings.where: The Settings page. The one place where precision beats warmth.

keys.general: Theme and language, plus the advanced toggles for haptics and wi-fi-only sync on Android. quietNotifications is about in-app toasts only; its description has to make clear that errors are still shown.
keys.ai: The extraction model: an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint the server calls to read a shared post. "Endpoint" and "model" are the technical words on purpose — the person filling these in is running a model. The key hint must say it is stored server-side and never shown again.
keys.advanced: Android-only sync switches. wifiOnly holds writes back until wi-fi; hidePausedStatus hides only the pill that reports that.
keys.data: Export, telemetry opt-out and account deletion. deleteAccount.confirmWord is what the user has to type to enable the destructive button — a short, unambiguous word in the target language, all lower case, and the dialog shows it literally. importDone and importInvalid report a restore: {{items}}, {{reviews}}, {{skipped}} and {{count}} are counts.
keys.region: The active region and the geocoder's monthly search pool. {{calls}}/{{limit}}/{{stopAt}} are numbers; "pool" is Amap's monthly allowance of place searches, and the app stops itself short of it.
keys.sources: The feeds the server polls. tier.A–M describe what a source costs (see the README's tier table); lastRun/lastFailed report a poll with {{when}} already formatted, {{found}}/{{created}} counts and {{error}} a translated error sentence.

keys.reauth_required: A server error code, rendered as a toast. The account deletion needs a sign-in only minutes old; this is what the user sees when confirming with Google did not produce one.
keys.crash: The last-resort error boundary. Its job is to reassure that nothing was lost — keep the promise that the data is safe on the device.
keys.codes: Server error codes rendered as toasts, keyed by the code the API answers with (geocode.quota, extract.not_configured, …). One sentence each, saying what happened and, where there is one, what to do.

security.where: Settings > Security, and the full-screen lock that replaces the whole app when a passcode is set. "Passcode" is the code the user chooses for this app, never the device PIN; "biometrics" is the phone fingerprint/face unlock.

price.where: How a ticket price from the feeds is shown: in list rows, the item sheet and the map hover card. The amount is already formatted with its currency symbol.

keys.free: The event costs nothing. One word, as on a ticket listing.
keys.from: The cheapest tier, with dearer ones above it — Chinese listings write 起 after the amount. {{price}} is the formatted amount, e.g. ¥39; place it where your language puts "from" (zh: ¥39起, ja: ¥39〜).

en.role: Reference language. Source strings are authored here and checkI18n compares every other locale against it.
en.plurals: one/other. Keys use the bare form for the singular plus `_other`.
en.register: Second person, contractions allowed, sentence case throughout — including buttons.

es.plurals: one/many/other. sync.offlinePending spells out all three; `_many` only matters from 1,000,000 and is omitted elsewhere.
es.register: Tú, never usted. Spain vocabulary (móvil, vale).
es.notes: The original language of the project — several English strings read as translations of these. Flavour text stays close to the English jokes.

it.plurals: one/many/other, same as Spanish. Bare form for the singular plus `_other`; `_many` given only for sync.offlinePending, matching the Spanish precedent.
it.register: Tu, informal. Sentence case. Guillemets «» for quoted names, matching Italian typographic convention rather than the straight quotes English uses.
it.gender: The hard constraint in this language. Both {{name}} and the reader have unknown gender, so several strings are deliberately restructured to dodge agreement: people.alsoKnownAs is "alias" rather than detto/detta; a checkup body says "al suo posto ci sia un Tamagotchi" instead of a participle agreeing with the person; "a {{name}} manchi" avoids inflecting on them entirely. Preserve that discipline when editing.
it.references: notifications.dailyReminderBodies quotes «Caro diario, oggi…», after Nanni Moretti's film. people.checkupBodies uses "visto e non risposto" (the seen-but-unanswered messaging culture), "colpo di scena", "Ultim'ora" and "Obiettivo sbloccato". Tamagotchi is kept.
it.terms: Entry = voce, sub-entry = sotto-voce, thread = filone, talking point = spunto, tag = etichetta, checkup = promemoria di contatto.

ja.plurals: Only `other` exists, so a single unsuffixed key covers every count and no `_other` variant is needed. Do not add `_one` — i18next will never select it, and a nicer singular wording (昨日終了 for "ended yesterday") is simply unreachable; people.eventEndedDaysAgo therefore uses the general 「{{count}}日前に終了」.
ja.register: です／ます, friendly but not stiff. Notifications lean casual with ね／よ endings. No 敬語 beyond that — this is the user's own diary talking to them, so humble/honorific forms would be wrong.
ja.counters: Counters are baked into the strings around {{count}}: 件 for entries and generic items, 人 for people, 個 for tags, 日 / 日間 for days, 歳 for age. Changing a noun means rechecking its counter.
ja.honorificOnNames: {{name}} is followed by さん in notifications and profile prose, which is the natural register. The trade-off is accepted knowingly: if a user stores a name that already ends in an honorific, it will double up. Names in this app are free text, most often given names, so さん is the better default.
ja.references: 三日坊主 (quitting on day three) for the daily reminder, 実績解除 and 段位 for the achievement joke, 既読スルー for the read-receipt joke, 音信不通 for radio silence, スタンプ (LINE stickers) in place of confetti emojis. たまごっち is kept and is native rather than a loan.
ja.typography: No spaces around 「」 or between Japanese and adjacent punctuation. A space goes either side of *literal* Latin runs (API キー) but deliberately not around interpolations: {{name}} may hold either a Latin or a Japanese name, and a hard-coded space would be wrong half the time. document.documentElement.lang is set on language change, which matters here — it tells the browser to pick Japanese rather than Chinese glyph forms for shared Han characters.
ja.terms: Entry = 記録, sub-entry = サブ記録, thread = スレッド, talking point = 話のネタ, tag = タグ, event = 出来事, checkup = 連絡リマインダー.

zh.script: Simplified (zh-Hans), targeting mainland usage. Registered as plain `zh`, so zh-CN/zh-SG resolve to it via nonExplicitSupportedLngs; a zh-Hant locale can be added later without touching anything else.
zh.plurals: Only `other` exists — single unsuffixed keys, exactly as in Japanese.
zh.register: 你, informal and direct. Sentence case is not a concept; keep punctuation full-width (：，。「」) except inside Latin runs.
zh.measureWords: Measure words sit around {{count}} in the strings: 条 for entries and talking points, 人 for people, 个 for tags and threads, 天 for days, 岁 for age, 件 for events. Changing a noun means rechecking its measure word.
zh.references: 断更／催更 (a serialised story going quiet, readers demanding more) and 打卡 (habit check-in) for the daily reminders; 电子宠物 for Tamagotchi; 已读不回 for the read-receipt joke; 潜水 for going silent; 表情包 and 「在吗」 for the send-something nudge; 成就解锁 for the achievement joke; 那年今日 for calendar.onThisDay.
zh.typography: A space goes either side of literal Latin runs and of numeric interpolations (Groq API 密钥, {{count}} 条记录) — standard Chinese typesetting, and what keeps an interpolated digit from fusing with a measure word. No space around {{name}}-style interpolations, though, since those may hold Han text and a hard-coded space would then be wrong.
zh.terms: Entry = 记录, sub-entry = 子记录, thread = 话题, talking point = 谈资, tag = 标签, event = 经历, checkup = 联系提醒. Note 线程 was rejected for thread: it means a CPU thread.
